title: .NET 11 Release Candidate 2: Go-Live License and Updates Across Libraries, F#, MAUI, and WinForms
gist: Microsoft released .NET 11 RC 2 with a go-live license, spanning libraries, runtime, SDK, NuGet, F#, ASP.NET Core, MAUI and Windows Forms, with no new C# language features. Highlights include experimental post-quantum crypto types, MSBuild speedups, NuGet package cooldowns and Reddit debate over odd-numbered release cadence.

insights.claim: Microsoft released .NET 11 RC 2 with a go-live license for production use, supported in Visual Studio 2026 Insiders and VS Code with C# Dev Kit, and with no new C# language features.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Production-supported RC signals GA is near and teams can begin migration testing.
insights.quote: Microsoft has released .NET 11 Release Candidate 2 with a go-live license for production use

insights.claim: Commenters note that since .NET 9 a standard-term release shares its end-of-support date with the preceding LTS, so moving to .NET 11 costs no support time.
insights.speaker: Reddit commenters
insights.so_what: The skip-odd-releases habit is no longer rational under the new support policy.
insights.quote: a standard-term release shares its end-of-support date with the preceding LTS version

insights.claim: Developers reported MAUI workloads breaking on every preview upgrade and questioned Blazor server-side rendering performance versus Razor Pages and MVC.
insights.speaker: Reddit commenters
insights.so_what: MAUI stability remains a recurring community pain point.

insights.claim: Two experimental cryptography types arrive, CompositeMLKem combining post-quantum and classical key encapsulation and Hpke with classical DHKEM suites only, both requiring opt-in diagnostics.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Hybrid post-quantum APIs in the mainstream .NET stack indicate enterprise preparation for PQC migration.
insights.quote: CompositeMLKem combines post-quantum and classical key encapsulation

insights.claim: NuGet adds --min-publish-age-hours to source commands and restore fails with NU1020 when a cooldown leaves no eligible floating version.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Package cooldowns are a supply-chain defense against freshly published malicious packages.

insights.claim: MSBuild gains faster wildcard matching, putting evaluation 10-13% faster with 16-34% fewer allocations in Microsoft's Windows benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Build performance gains compound across large solutions and CI.

insights.claim: CoreCLR disables advisory file locking by default on iOS and tvOS because FileStream locking in RC 1 could cause the OS to terminate an app entering the background; this is the one runtime breaking change.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Apple platform quirks drive runtime behavior changes late in the cycle.
insights.quote: FileStream lock in RC 1 could cause the OS to terminate an app entering the background
insights.locator: The runtime release focuses on reliability

insights.claim: ASP.NET Core changes are mostly removals and renames for RC 1 upgraders, such as replacing IValidationMessageFormatter with FormatMessage and pulling the experimental device-bound sessions package.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Upgraders must adapt even between RCs.
insights.locator: ASP.NET Core has few new features

insights.claim: F# ships preview return and await intrinsics for custom computation-expression builders on the runtime-async model, though FSharp.Core does not yet ship such a builder.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Runtime-async support is expanding to F# but tooling is incomplete.
insights.quote: though FSharp.Core does not yet ship such a builder

insights.claim: MAUI adds a --ui csharp template option, an --avalonia desktop option, Android API 37.2 and JDK 25 support, and Apple workloads now require Xcode 27.0 with UIKit scene lifecycle adoption.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: MAUI is broadening toward code-first UI and third-party desktop targets.

insights.claim: New Windows Forms analyzers WFO3000 to WFO3002 flag code that cannot round-trip through the Designer, which the notes call particularly useful when AI tools generate or refactor forms.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Tooling is adapting to AI-generated UI code that violates designer constraints.
insights.quote: particularly useful when AI tools generate or refactor forms
